_desc: ★ THE R3 GATE FOR §3/T6 (spec 2026-07-27-team-plane-static-parity-routing-design, owner ruling §11): a TEAM-plane message must not generate a STATIC-plane frame. This is the ONE configuration s35a/s35b cannot cover — they are OFF-GRID only (which is exactly why their A2/A4 are labelled algebra-only in-file), and the defect T6 fixes only exists for a HOMED member. 4 nodes on ONE PHY, ONE leaf nibble (mixed-leaf is s29/s35a's axis, not this one). ★ THE LOAD-BEARING TOPOLOGY, and every link is deliberate: TH is a HOMED member (it hears H1, registers, and its _node_id becomes the host-assigned mobile local id while its team id stays 210); TO is an OFF-GRID member with NO LINK TO H1 AT ALL, so at the moment of the first ack TO holds no static route to 101 — TH is is_mobile, so route_uses_mobile_as_transit refuses it as static transit. That absence is the whole experiment: it converts the pre-T6 plane crossing from a silent success into a LOUD, countable failure. ⚠ CORRECTED 2026-07-28 (§team-parity T8), because the original wording said TO 'cannot acquire one' and that is FALSE: S2↔TO exists and S2 advertises 101 at hops 1, so once anything makes S2's table dirty enough to beacon, TO learns rt_update{dest:101,hops:2,next:102}. In the CLEAN run that never happens — H1 and S2 skip every beacon as beacon_max_idle_skip_clean, so the static plane never converges at all and TO emits no dest-101 rt_update — but under P-T6A the ack's own storm makes S2 beacon and TO does acquire it (measured, t=214260). The experiment is unaffected (the first ack's r_tx fires at ttl 1 well before), but do not rely on the absence being structural. Pre-T6 (measured 2026-07-28, BASELINE SCEN note): stamp_origin gave a homed member's team DM origin = its HOME's STATIC id 101, the acking teammate took origin as its ack destination and addressed 101 on the STATIC plane — r_tx{dst:101,reason:no_route} at ttl 1 then ttl 16 x3 (FOUR static RREQ floods generated by a TEAM message's ack), send_deferred_giveup, then send_failed{e2e_ack_timeout} on TH at +60 s. Post-T6 the origin is 210, AUTO dispatches it to _rt_team via is_team_peer, and the ack returns on the team plane in ~1 s with zero static frames. ★ THE CONTROL ARM IS TO->TH (asserts 20-23), the off-grid direction, which worked BEFORE T6 and must still work AFTER: without it a green run could not distinguish 'T6 fixed the homed case' from 'the acks happen to work now'. ⚠ TWO AUTHORING TRAPS, both hit while building this file. (1) team_dad_pin_id is REQUIRED, not cosmetic: without it team-DAD picks uniformly at random from 17..254, so no assertion could name an origin id and the R3 assertion could not be written at all. It pins only the FIRST pick (node_mobile.cpp:188) and a re-pick still randomises, so convergence is untouched. (2) `-t` is a TRAILING suffix on both send verbs (sim NodeRuntimeWrapper, committed 8135912) — the prefix form silently airs '-t <text>' as the BODY on plane AUTO, which is the defect that was live in s23:25/31/37/43 until 2026-07-28. ⚠ DO NOT read `rt_update.slot` in any analysis of this file: node_beacon.cpp:876/879 label a beacon-DV merge primary/alt regardless of which TABLE was merged, so a same-team beacon's merge into _rt_team reads slot=primary (sim-only telemetry defect, reported not fixed). ⚠ THE `routes` COMMAND AT 400000 ms IS DEAD: the sim's console has NO `routes` verb (NodeRuntimeWrapper parses send/send_e2e/send_hash/send_hashx/send_layer*/send_channel*/reqpubkey/team/join/leave only), so it replies 'ERROR: unparsed command'. The claim that asserts 16/17 read a route dump was never true — 16 keys on e2e_ack_tx and 17 on rts_tx. Left in place rather than removed (removing it is a separate stream edit); reported 2026-07-28. ASSERT LABELS: 1-4 setup (the homed/off-grid split is REAL, not assumed), 5-9 the T6 origin namespace, 10-19 ★ R3 (the ack returns on the team plane and NO static-plane frame is generated), 21-24 the off-grid control arm, 25-28 ★★ the R3/I2 DIRECT detectors added by §team-parity T8. ★★ PROBE MATRIX — RE-MEASURED 2026-07-28 (§team-parity T8) against this exact file, by reverting T6/Part A's stamp_origin team arm to the pre-T6 expression (probe P-T6A). ⚠ THE MATRIX RECORDED BY T6 (801 events / 12 of 24) IS STALE AND ITS LAPSE IS THE REASON 25-28 EXIST: §team-parity T7 removed the is_team_peer(origin) fence on the DATA-origin learn, which silently narrowed this probe to **729 events / 9 of 24** — asserts 13, 14 and 20 STOPPED DISCRIMINATING, including the one labelled ★★ THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION. MECHANISM, measured: under P-T6A the origin is the static 101, and the unfenced learn installs rt_update{dest:101,hops:1,next:210,slot:team} on TO from the frame it is acking (learn_route_via:73 also sets the _team_peer[101] dispatch bit), so rt_find(101,AUTO) resolves on _rt_team, TO holds a route, no r_tx is ever raised and the absent-RREQ symptom disappears while the breach gets WORSE — the ack is routed TO→TH→H1 and the HOME consumes it (e2e_ack_rx + push{kind:e2e_acked} on H1 for a DM it never sent). CURRENT MATRIX, all three arms measured on the same file: CLEAN = 654 events, 0 failures · **P-T6A (T7 live) = 729 events, 12 of 28 FAIL** (5,6,7,8,9 origin namespace · 11,12 the ack · 16,19 the ack's addressing/count · ★ 25,26,28 the new direct detectors) · **P-T6A + P-T7 (T7's fence restored, i.e. the tree T6 was gated on) = 801 events, 16 of 28 FAIL** = the same 5,6,7,8,9,11,12,16,19 plus the original symptom trio 13,14,20 (all twelve the T6 note recorded, reproduced EXACTLY) plus all four new detectors 25,26,27,28 — which is the proof that T7, not this file's authoring, caused the lapse. ⚠ 13/14/20 CANNOT be repaired in place and are deliberately KEPT anyway: they assert the absence of an r_tx, and under the T7-live shape no r_tx genuinely happens, so no form of an r_tx-keyed assertion can fire. 25-28 re-arm the PROPERTY those three measured (R3: a team message pulls no static infrastructure into its path) by keying on the frame's ARRIVAL at the static host and on the route table, not on the absence of a route request. Keeping both means a future slice that masks one shape still trips the other — which is the whole lesson of the lapse. ★ ALL FOUR control-arm assertions (21-24) HOLD under both probes — that is what makes them a control rather than a second copy of the experiment. ⚠ ASSERTS 17 and 18 HOLD UNDER P-T6A TOO and are NOT discriminators — they are standing invariants, recorded honestly: 17 holds because TO's own control-arm DM also RTSes to 210, and 18 because a static route request is a broadcast F, never an RTS. Do not cite either as evidence that T6 works.

commands._c: ★ THE MEASURED CASE: a HOMED member's TEAM-plane -a send. Trailing ' -t' is the only form the parser honours.
CONTROL ARM: the OFF-GRID direction, which already worked pre-T6 and must not regress.
second homed -a, after both directions have converged (the ack path must be repeatable, not first-flight luck)
the route dump asserts 16/17 read (a cmd_reply assertion needs the command to have actually been issued)

expect._c: 1 [setup] TH is genuinely HOMED onto the static host 101 - the precondition for the whole defect
2 [setup] TH's team id is the pinned 210, so every id below is nameable
3 [setup] TO's team id is the pinned 220
4 [setup] ★ TO is genuinely OFF-GRID: it never adopts a home (no link to H1, autoregister off)
5 [T6 origin] ★ THE SLICE: the homed member stamps its TEAM id 210, not its home's STATIC id 101 (pre-T6: origin=101)
6 [T6 origin] ★ and NEVER 101 - one origin namespace per plane, for every -t send in the run
7 [T6 origin] the receiver sees the team id on the wire (inner origin), not the home id
8 [T6 origin] ★ the receiver NEVER sees 101 as a team-DM origin (pre-T6 this was the only value it saw)
9 [T6 origin] delivery carries the team origin all the way to the app push
10 [T6 origin] the SECOND homed -a arrives too (same origin namespace on a repeat send)

11 [R3] ★ the E2E ack RETURNS to the homed sender (pre-T6 it never did in this topology). NB the push kind is `e2e_acked`, not `send_e2e_acked` - the sim renders the firmware's own PushKind table (NodeRuntimeWrapper drainPushes)

12 [R3] ★ and NO ack ever times out on TH (pre-T6: send_failed{e2e_ack_timeout} at +60 s). ⚠ ASSERTED ON THE `send_failed` EMIT, NOT ON THE PUSH, and that is load-bearing: the sim's push emit carries only ctr/dst/kind and DROPS the reason string (slice-gate-method §E, a documented structural blind spot), so a push-keyed form of this assertion would have been unmovable decoration. Measured: keyed on the emit it fails under P-T6A, keyed on the push it does not.

13 [R3] ★★ THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION: the acking teammate generates ZERO route requests for the HOME's static id. Pre-T6 this was r_tx{dst:101,reason:no_route} at ttl 1 then ttl 16 x3 - four STATIC-plane RREQ floods produced by a TEAM message's ack, which is the R3 violation ('team-internal routing only, no static infrastructure in the path').
14 [R3] ★ no static-plane RREQ is FORWARDED for the home's id either - the flood is absent, not merely unanswered
15 [R3] the acking teammate does not give up a deferred send (pre-T6: send_deferred_giveup for dst 101)
16 [R3] the ack is emitted as a DM addressed to the sender's TEAM id 210 (e2e_ack_tx carries `dst`, not `to`)

17 [R3] ★ the ack's FIRST HOP is the team id 210 - it left on the team plane, not toward static infrastructure. Deliberately NOT asserted via rt_update.slot: node_beacon.cpp:876/879 mislabel a beacon-DV team merge as slot=primary, so `slot` cannot prove which table a write landed in (BASELINE SCEN finding).
18 [R3] ★ TO never addresses the HOME as a next hop, on any frame in the run - 101 stays invisible to the member (I2)
19 [R3] BOTH homed -a sends are acked (ctr 1 and ctr 3) - the path is stable, not a first-flight coincidence. Counted on e2e_ack_rx because an ack push carries no payload to match on.

20 [R3] ★ zero static route requests of ANY kind on the acking teammate across the whole run: a team-plane message generates no static-plane frame at all, which is the criterion stated more strongly than 'not for dst 101'

25 [R3-direct] ★★ THE RESTORED ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (added 2026-07-28, §team-parity T8). Asserts 13/14/20 key on a DOWNSTREAM SYMPTOM - the ABSENCE of static-plane route requests - and T7 silently masked all three: with the DATA-origin learn unfenced, TO installs rt_update{dest:101,hops:1,next:210,slot:team} from the very frame it is acking, so it HOLDS a route to 101, emits no r_tx at all, and the symptom vanishes while the breach gets WORSE. This assertion keys on the breach's DESTINATION instead: the home CONSUMES its hosted mobile's teammate's E2E ack as its own (push{kind:e2e_acked} on H1 for a DM it never sent). MEASURED under P-T6A: 1 with T7 live, 2 with T7's fence restored - it FAILS IN BOTH SHAPES, which is exactly what 13/14/20 could not do. ★ WHY IT CANNOT BE MASKED THE WAY 13/14/20 WERE: masking a not_contains needs the forbidden thing to stop happening, and the only two ways for H1 to stop seeing the ack are (a) the ack routes team-internally - the correct behaviour - or (b) no ack is generated at all, which asserts 11 and 19 fail on. The PAIR (11+19 'the ack must reach TH') AND (25+26 'H1 must never see it') can both pass ONLY if the ack travelled inside the team plane. That pairing is what 13/14/20 lacked: 'no RREQ' is satisfiable by routing the frame somewhere else.

26 [R3-direct] ★ the frame-level twin of 25: NO DATA frame of the team exchange is ever accepted by the static host - the R3 wording ('no static infrastructure in the path') asserted on the path itself rather than on a route request. s37 contains no static DM, so any data_rx on H1 is a team frame. MEASURED under P-T6A: 1 with T7 live, 2 with the T7 fence restored - fails in both shapes.

27 [R3-direct] and no team frame is RELAYED by the other static node either. Complements 25/26 by shape rather than duplicating them: MEASURED under P-T6A this is 0 with T7 live (the ack goes TO->TH->H1, never through S2) and 2 with the T7 fence restored (S2 relays the ack it answered the RREQ for, emitting its own push{kind:send_acked} for dst 101). So 25/26 catch the ROUTED shape and 27 catches the FLOODED shape.

28 [I2/A2-direct] ★ the invariant stated POSITIVELY instead of by symptom: the home's static id never becomes a routing destination on the off-grid member. Under P-T6A with T7 live the leak is rt_update{dest:101,hops:1,next:210,score:10.5,slot:team} - a STATIC node id inside _rt_team, spec A2 breached, and learn_route_via:73 sets the _team_peer[101] dispatch bit with it. This is the route-table twin of assert 18 ('101 stays invisible to the member'). ⚠ DELIBERATELY NOT keyed on slot, per the SCEN finding that node_beacon.cpp:876/879 mislabel team merges as primary - a slot-keyed form would be silently disarmed the day that mislabel is fixed, and would already miss any breach arriving via the beacon-DV path. ⚠ HONEST SCOPE, so nobody over-reads it: matching only on dest, it does NOT distinguish _rt_team from _rt, so it ALSO forbids a legitimate STATIC route to 101. That is over-strict by design (over-strict fails loud; under-strict passes silently) and it costs nothing here: in the clean run TO emits no dest-101 rt_update at all. MEASURED under P-T6A: 2 leaks with T7 live (the slot:team breach at t=200739 FIRST, then a static DV route via 102 at t=214260) and 1 with the T7 fence restored - fails in both shapes.
21 [control] the off-grid member's own origin is its team id 220 (unchanged by T6 - node_id == team_local_id off-grid)
22 [control] the homed member receives the off-grid teammate's DM
23 [control] ★ the off-grid direction's ack returns too - this arm held BEFORE T6, which is what makes it a control
24 [control] and the homed member's ack for it goes to the off-grid TEAM id 220, never to a static id

★★ 29 §team-parity T5 — WHY THE HEARD-SET SCAN'S SELF-ID MUST BE PLANE-SELECTED, and this scenario is the ONLY place in the corpus that can say it. TH is the HOMED member, so its static node_id (host-assigned 254) and its team_local_id (210) are DIFFERENT values — the dual split s35a/s35b cannot express because every member there is off-grid. A teammate's route page advertises TEAM ids, so the scan must look for 210. Presence half: TH correctly finds itself in TO's page and records CONFIRMED.

★★ 30 — the ABSENCE half, PAIRED with 29 per the T8 rule: TH must NEVER conclude its link to TO is one-way. A plane-blind scan (looking for _node_id 254 instead of team_local_id 210) never finds itself, so a HEALTHY team link is falsely demoted on EVERY homed member — measured: this exact edit turns 22 confirms into a one_way plus 7 degraded_advertise beacons. 29 forbids that being masked by the scan simply not running.

31 — the downstream consequence of 30: a false one-way verdict would be GOSSIPED as a degraded route page entry. Zero degraded advertisements is the observable that the homed member's own view is healthy.

32 — invariant I8 on the R3 scenario: the two STATIC nodes never take the team bidi arm at all. H1 deliberately cannot even reach TO (see the _desc), which is what makes this the strongest isolation ground in the corpus.
33 — and the id form: a team local id (210 = TH, 220 = TO) must never appear in a STATIC node's bidi verdict, which is a write into the node_id-indexed _link_bidi[256] (invariant I2).
